text:
Sentence 1: Indicate the continent where the Amazon Rainforest is located.
- Indicate: prefix in- (not/into) + root dic (say/show) + suffix -ate (verb form)
- continent: root cont (together) + suffix -in (state/condition) + suffix -ent (noun form)
- where: root wh- (question word) + suffix -ere (adverbial form)
- Amazon: proper noun (no affixes)
- Rainforest: root rain + root forest (compound word)
- located: root loc (place) + suffix -at (verb form) + suffix -ed (past tense/participle)

Sentence 2: Interdisciplinary studies bridge the gap between traditional academic boundaries.
- Interdisciplinary: prefix inter- (between/among) + root discipline + suffix -ary (adjective form)
- studies: root stud (study) + suffix -ies (plural noun)
- bridge: root bridge (noun/verb)
- gap: root gap (noun)
- between: prefix be- (around/through) + root tween (two) + suffix -en (verb form)
- traditional: root trad (hand over) + suffix -ition (noun form) + suffix -al (adjective form)
- academic: root acad (Academy/school) + suffix -emic (adjective form)
- boundaries: root bound (limit) + suffix -ary (noun form) + suffix -ies (plural noun)

Sentence 3: The prefix 'inter-' means between or among, while the root 'discipline' refers to a branch of knowledge or learning.
- prefix: root pre- (before) + root fix (fasten)
- means: root mean (measure/way) + suffix -s (plural noun/third person singular)
- between: prefix be- + root tween + suffix -en
- among: root a- (on/in) + root mong (middle)
- while: root wh- + root ile (time/period)
- root: root roo (base) + suffix -t (noun form)
- discipline: root discip (teach/learn) + suffix -ine (noun form)
- refers: root fer (bring/carry) + suffix -er (agent/noun) + suffix -s (third person singular)
- branch
